Read an image's header and metadata

Source: R/info.R
pix_info.Rd

Reports what an image is without decoding its pixels: format, size, depth, colour type, transparency, interlacing, animation, density, EXIF orientation, PNG colour chunks, and whether ICC and EXIF data are present. The colour information is reported, never applied.

Usage

pix_info(x, format = "auto", limits = pix_limits())

Arguments

x

File paths (one row each), a raw vector holding one file's bytes, or a connection, which is read whole.

format

"auto" reads the format from the file's signature, never its extension. A named format ("png", "jpeg", "webp", "qoi") that disagrees with the signature is an error.

limits

Limits checked before anything is allocated; see pix_limits().

Value

A data frame with one row per image and columns:

  • format: "png", "jpeg", "webp" or "qoi".

  • width, height: in pixels, as stored (before any EXIF rotation).

  • bits: the stored sample depth: 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 for PNG; the precision for JPEG (8, or 12 which zupix does not decode); 8 otherwise.

  • colour_type: "grey", "grey_alpha", "rgb", "rgba", "palette", "ycbcr", "cmyk" or "ycck", as stored. JPEG and lossy WebP store YCbCr; CMYK and YCCK JPEG decode to RGB.

  • alpha: whether the image has transparency, including PNG tRNS.

  • interlaced: Adam7 PNG or progressive JPEG.

  • animated: APNG or animated WebP; pix_read() decodes the first frame.

  • density_x, density_y, density_unit: from PNG pHYs (unit 1: pixels per metre) or the JPEG JFIF header (1: per inch, 2: per centimetre); unit 0 gives only the aspect ratio. NA when absent.

  • orientation: the EXIF orientation, 1 to 8, or NA. See pix_orient().

  • gamma, srgb: PNG gAMA (the stored value over 100,000) and the sRGB rendering intent, or NA.

  • chrm: a list column, PNG cHRM's eight chromaticities (white, red, green, blue; x then y), or NULL.

  • cicp: a list column, PNG cICP's four integers (colour primaries, transfer function, matrix coefficients, full-range flag), or NULL.

  • icc, exif: whether an ICC profile or EXIF data is present; see pix_icc() and pix_exif().

  • qoi_linear: for QOI, whether the header declares linear channels rather than sRGB; NA for other formats.

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "gradient.png", package = "zupix")
pix_info(f)
#>   format width height bits colour_type alpha interlaced animated density_x
#> 1    png    48     32    8         rgb FALSE      FALSE    FALSE        NA
#>   density_y density_unit orientation gamma srgb chrm cicp   icc  exif
#> 1        NA           NA          NA    NA   NA NULL NULL FALSE FALSE
#>   qoi_linear
#> 1         NA
